prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1190; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling westbound on a residential roadway in Baytown, Texas, when the front of the vehicle struck the front of a vehicle driven by Driver 2, which was traveling eastbound in the same lane. The impact was low speed, but both vehicles sustained front-end damage consistent with the reported collision. Driver 2 confirmed at the scene that the collision occurred as Driver 1 described it. Two witnesses gave statements that matched this account, and photographs taken at the scene show damage that lines up with the point and direction of impact. No prior damage to either vehicle was noted by those present or identified in available records. A passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time, and officers and witnesses confirmed that person's presence. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder, which responding personnel observed was consistent with the forces involved in the collision. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy covering the vehicle involved. No citations were issued at the scene.
